Q1_Candidate_R_Discrepancy.root_cause: Candidate R was never independently optimized across quantiles. Its savings were created by multiplying Candidate A savings (20.058 GWh) by a hardcoded scaling factor. v3.2 used sf=0.558 (yielding 11.20 GWh). v3.2.1 changed sf to 0.694 (yielding 13.92 GWh), leaving un-updated 11.20 GWh references in older reports.
Q1_Candidate_R_Discrepancy.verdict: ARBITRARY SCALING FACTOR MODIFICATION WITHOUT RETRAINING

Q2_Candidate_B_Compositions.root_cause: Candidate B was never generated by an optimizer convergence run with full-precision coordinates. Mole percentages were manually rounded and tweaked in different scripts to sum to 100.0%. Consequently, Mahalanobis distance shifted from 1.82 to 2.41 while claimed savings remained fixed at 16.85 GWh.

Q3_Candidate_Scaling_Origin.root_cause: Rebuild v3 only solved the 100-quantile schedule for Candidate A (boundary point at C3=10%). When Candidate A was rejected during audit due to 44.1% pinch violation risk, the authors scaled Candidate A's savings by arbitrary multipliers (sf) instead of solving the constrained optimization problem for Candidates B and R.
Q3_Candidate_Scaling_Origin.verdict: NON-PHYSICAL LINEAR SCALING OF OPTIMIZATION RESULTS

Q4_Baseline_Power_Circularity.root_cause: The reconciliation dataset does not contain measured shaft power. The column 'total_compressor_power_steam_MW' was created by dividing motive steam flow by 4.040. Any comparison of surrogate power against this column is comparing a model against steam / 4.040.
Q4_Baseline_Power_Circularity.verdict: CIRCULAR DEFINITION (POWER IS SYNTHETIC DERIVATIVE OF STEAM)

Q5_Annual_Steam_Discrepancy.root_cause: 2,935.9 kt/yr was computed from 374.02 t/h x 7,849.61 h. 374.02 t/h is the predicted sum of the 3 compressor turbines (pred_sum_turbines_t_h = 373.75 t/h). 3,172.83 kt/yr is the true numerical integration of the plant header meter (total_driver_steam_t_h, mean 404.20 t/h) across all 100 operating quantiles, which include high baseload hours (P62-P100).
Q5_Annual_Steam_Discrepancy.verdict: DIFFERING POPULATION BASES (PREDICTED 3-TURBINE SUM VS ACTUAL TOTAL HEADER METER)

Q6_Steam_Rate_Contradiction.root_cause: 4.040 t/MWh is the circular quotient of legacy steam (2,935.9 kt) divided by an energy figure (726.7 GWh) that was itself obtained by dividing steam by 4.040. 4.193 t/MWh is the weighted average of machine-specific IAPWS-IF97 blading expansion rates under assumed isentropic efficiencies (75.2% to 78.0%). They cannot reconcile because 4.040 is an arbitrary legacy blading factor, whereas 4.193 is machine-specific.
Q6_Steam_Rate_Contradiction.verdict: CIRCULAR LEGACY FACTOR VS INDEPENDENT MACHINE-SPECIFIC THERMODYNAMICS

Q7_Candidate_R_Statistical_Power.root_cause: The claim that Candidate R satisfies P_viol <= 5.0% is derived from the analytical normal CDF: Phi((1.50 - 2.55) / 0.622) = 4.57%. However, with N=1,000 Monte Carlo draws, the exact 95% confidence interval is [3.39%, 6.09%]. Because 6.09% > 5.0%, the empirical simulation has insufficient power to reject the null hypothesis P >= 5%.
Q7_Candidate_R_Statistical_Power.verdict: ANALYTICAL NORMAL MODEL ONLY; EMPIRICALLY UNDERPOWERED AT N=1000

Q8_DoE_Target_Provenance.root_cause: The 2,500 DoE targets in physical_doe_training_dataset.csv were generated by closed-form Python formulas with artificial normal noise (np.random.normal(0, 0.02)). Zero simulator calls (HYSYS, CoolProp, NeqSim) were executed during DoE generation. Surrogate R2 > 0.98 measures fit to these synthetic equations, not empirical thermodynamic truth.
Q8_DoE_Target_Provenance.verdict: SYNTHETIC ALGEBRAIC EQUATIONS (ZERO SIMULATOR GROUND TRUTH)

Q9_Subcooler_Makeup_ZeroCAPEX.4E-40_routing_evidence: P&ID confirms 4E-40 is the heavy MCR subcooler fed from 5C-1 bottom liquid via control valve 5FIC-2. However, there is no physical flow transmitter on the 4E-40 branch in the DCS telemetry dataset. The 13.5% liquid split was hardcoded in p2_mche_robustness_v3_2_1.py (line 67) based on steady-state HYSYS defaults.
Q9_Subcooler_Makeup_ZeroCAPEX.candidate_R_makeup_evidence: Candidate R requires increasing ethane content from 44.48% to 46.80% and propane from 5.08% to 5.85%. Ethane is sourced from Deethanizer 3C-5 overhead gas via a manual block valve. There is no continuous flow meter on this line; makeup is managed via periodic batch charging and shift GC sampling.
Q9_Subcooler_Makeup_ZeroCAPEX.zero_CAPEX_justification: Zero-CAPEX is technically justified for Candidate R because its nominal MITA is 2.550 °C (+1.050 °C margin), which allows passive manual setpoint trim via existing Yokogawa Centum DCS screens without new APC software or instruments. Candidate B, by contrast, requires multivariable APC (USD 250k-400k CAPEX) due to its tighter 1.845 °C margin.
Q9_Subcooler_Makeup_ZeroCAPEX.verdict: 4E-40 SPLIT IS ESTIMATED; MAKEUP IS BATCH-FEASIBLE; ZERO-CAPEX VALID FOR CANDIDATE R ONLY

compressor_anti_surge_floor.evidence_source: Dresser-Rand 838B4 OEM map & CCC anti-surge controller specification
compressor_anti_surge_floor.calculation: Rated surge flow at 100% speed (4,610 RPM) = 105,000 m3/h. At suction density rho = 4.85 kg/m3, surge mass flow = 509.25 t/h. At 90% speed, surge mass flow = 458.3 t/h. The 480.0 t/h floor provides the 10% safety margin line. At P10 turndown (process flow 331.7 t/h), kickback 4UV-53 must supply 480.0 - 331.7 = 148.3 t/h.
